content: 1. Exercise caution when rilpivirine is co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes, as this can increase the risk of QTc interval prolongation. 2. Itraconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. No dose adjustment for rilpivirine is required, but monitoring is recommended. 3. Both itraconazole and rilpivirine can prolong the QTc interval, necessitating careful monitoring. 4. Ketoconazole also increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is needed, but monitoring is advised. 5. When azole antifungals are co-administered with rilpivirine, monitor for breakthrough fungal infections. 6. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of lapatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Levofloxacin co-administration with rilpivirine increases the risk of QTc prolongation and toxicity. Monitor patients carefully. 8. Levoketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required, but monitoring is necessary. 9. Magnesium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine can significantly reduce rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to increased gastric pH. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 11. Magnesium gluconate and magnesium oxide similarly decrease rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 12. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or 6 hours after administration. 13. Magnesium sulfate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 14. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of maprotiline by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Mavorixafor increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring and potential therapy modification. 16. Mefloquine co-administration with rilpivirine increases the risk of QTc prolongation and toxicity. Monitor patients carefully. 17. Methadone co-administration with rilpivirine does not require dose adjustments, but rilpivirine increases methadone toxicity via QTc prolongation. Monitor closely. 18. Mirtazapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 19. Moxifloxacin increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Monitor patients closely. 20. Nefazodone increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Nizatidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH, potentially leading to treatment failure or resistance. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 24. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of nortriptyline by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Rilpivirine increases octreotide toxicity via QTc prolongation. Monitor patients carefully. 26. Olanzapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Orlistat decreases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, potentially leading to virological failure. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 28. Osilodrostat and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Ozanimod and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients on QT-prolonging drugs. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. 30.
